stock_segments.discussion_summary: Tele2 reported inline earnings but stock fell 7%. The hosts believe the drop is due to concerns about Sweden banning Huawei/ZTE from 5G networks, which will make network expansion more expensive for operators. However, this ban benefits Ericsson. Wolf bought the dip, noting that institutional investors seem to be selling before the election. They expect the stock to recover post-election as the market re-evaluates. Discussion also covers 5G rollout in Sweden vs USA, with Sweden expected to roll out more broadly even if starting later.

stock_segments.discussion_summary: Saab issued a profit warning due to supply chain delays and coronavirus impacts. The stock has underperformed despite having strong technology and a large order book. The hosts note that ESG funds and AP funds have sold the stock. Wolf believes Saab is cheap, especially around 170 SEK levels seen during the pandemic. The challenge is the long time horizon - order book spans 5-6 years, which makes it hard for the stock market to value properly. The company has significant value in patents and technology not being capitalized. Discussion covers potential takeover but notes national security concerns would limit foreign buyers. The recommendation is to buy as an alternative to savings if you can hold for several years.
